facts.fact: The page 'Branded content vs sponsored content: What's the difference?' was published on 13 October 2015.
Branded content tends to be produced in-house by the brand, while sponsored content is usually a collaborative effort between the publisher's editorial staff and the brand.
facts.quote: While branded content tends to be produced in-house by the brand, sponsored content is usually a collaborative effort between the publisher’s editorial staff and the brand.

facts.fact: Branded content lives on brand-owned properties such as micro-sites or content hubs, while sponsored content is hosted on the publisher's site and therefore reaches the publisher's audience.
facts.quote: while branded content lives on brand-owned properties such as micro-sites or content hubs

facts.fact: Under the sponsored content model, a brand commissions a publisher both to produce the content and to publish it on the publisher's website.
facts.quote: they commission a publisher to both produce the content and to publish it on their website.

facts.fact: Branded content reaches the brand's audience, while sponsored content reaches the publisher's audience.
facts.quote: Branded content reaches the brand’s audience, while sponsored content reaches the publisher’s audience.

facts.fact: As a sponsored content example, Cole Haan commissioned The New York Times' T Brand Studio to promote its new collection of ballet flats, producing the feature 'Grit and Grace'.
facts.quote: Cole Haan commissioned T Brand Studio to promote its new collection of ballet flats.

facts.fact: Brands and publishers typically avoid a 'salesy' tone in sponsored and branded content strategy, focusing instead on educational or entertaining content.
facts.quote: brands and publishers typically avoid a ‘salesy’ tone. Rather, they focus on delivering educational or entertaining content to readers.
